question.worked_solution:
The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{f({x}_{n})}{{f}^{′}({x}_{n})}
$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ is the derivative of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=({x}^{3}+4x-6)^{′}=3{x}^{2}+4.
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{{x}_{n}^{3}+4{x}_{n}-6}{3{x}_{n}^{2}+4} \\  & =\frac{{x}_{n}(3{x}_{n}^{2}+4)-({x}_{n}^{3}+4{x}_{n}-6)}{3{x}_{n}^{2}+4} \\  & =\frac{2{x}_{n}^{3}+6}{3{x}_{n}^{2}+4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=1.3,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{2{x}_{0}^{3}+6}{3{x}_{0}^{2}+4} \\  & =\frac{2(1.3)^{3}+6}{3(1.3)^{2}+4} \\  & =1.145…\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\frac{2{x}_{1}^{3}+6}{3{x}_{1}^{2}+4} \\  & =\frac{2(1.145…)^{3}+6}{3(1.145…)^{2}+4} \\  & =1.134…, \\ {x}_{3} & =\frac{2{x}_{2}^{3}+6}{3{x}_{2}^{2}+4} \\  & =\frac{2(1.134…)^{3}+6}{3(1.134…)^{2}+4} \\  & =1.134….\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the last two approximations ${x}_{2}≈1.13$ and ${x}_{3}≈1.13$ are the same when rounded to two decimal places.

Therefore, the root of the function is $x≈1.13,$ rounded to two decimal places.
